question: What is the thick middle layer of the heart wall called?
explanation: The myocardium is the muscular middle layer responsible for the pumping action of the heart. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why does the heart have a muscular wall (septum) right down its middle?

options.A: To provide extra structural support for blood vessels
options.B: To help anchor the valves in place securely
options.C: To slow down the heart rate during rest
options.D: To keep oxygen-rich and oxygen-poor blood from mixing

explanation: Well done! The septum acts like a solid divider, ensuring clean, oxygenated blood stays separate from the used blood. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h1)

question: Where does the right side of the heart pump deoxygenated blood?
explanation: The right ventricle sends oxygen-poor blood through the pulmonary arteries to the lungs for gas exchange. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h2)

question: If a patient has a weak left ventricle, which part of circulation is affected first?
explanation: Great thinking! The left ventricle pumps blood into the aorta to feed the rest of the body, which is our systemic circulation. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h2)

question: What happens in the heart to create the first heart sound (the 'lub' of 'lub-dub')?
explanation: You nailed it! That first sound is simply the AV valves slamming shut to stop blood from flowing backward when the ventricles squeeze. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h3)

question: What happens in the heart during ventricular diastole?

options.B: The heart muscle rests without any blood flow
options.C: The ventricles contract and eject blood
options.D: The ventricles relax and fill with blood

explanation: Diastole is the relaxation phase where the heart chambers fill up with blood before the next contraction. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h3)

question: Which structure acts as the primary natural pacemaker of the heart?
explanation: The SA node has the fastest rate of spontaneous depolarization, setting the pace for normal heart contractions. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h4)

question: Why is there a tiny electrical pause when the signal reaches the AV node?

options.A: To give the SA node time to recharge its energy
options.B: To allow the upper chambers (atria) to finish emptying into the lower chambers
options.C: To prevent the heart from beating too slowly
options.D: To direct blood straight into the heart muscles

explanation: Brilliant! That little pause gives the atria just enough time to squeeze all their blood down into the ventricles first. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h4)

question: On an ECG machine, what does the tall QRS complex show us?
explanation: You've got it! The QRS wave shows the electrical spark rushing through the big lower chambers right before they pump. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h5)

question: Which wave on a normal ECG tracing shows the ventricles recovering and resetting?
explanation: Spot on! The T wave is the visual sign of the heart muscle cells recharging and getting ready for the next beat. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h5)
